I read the whole file. It has no new definitions or structures. It contains instances and lemmas.

The one near-duplicate I found is `Subgroup.toIsOrderedMonoid`. `SubmonoidClass.toIsOrderedMonoid` in Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Monoid/Submonoid.lean (priority 75) applies to subgroups through the subgroup class instances, so it covers the same case. Mathlib already follows this pattern for `Submonoid.toIsOrderedMonoid`, and a comment there says "Prefer subclasses of `Monoid` over subclasses of `SubmonoidClass`". The Subgroup instance is therefore a deliberate, conventional specialisation, not a competing concept. I did not check whether removing it would break instance search.

I also checked these:
- `IsModularLattice (Subgroup C)` is the only such instance I found for Subgroup.
- `isCoatom_comap` and `isCoatom_map` are one-line applications of `OrderIso.isCoatom_iff`, so they are named specialisations. They are also standalone theorems, which the rubric excludes.
- `mabs_mem_iff`, the strictMono lemmas and `NormalizerCondition.normal_of_coatom` are theorems, not competing concepts.

I found no justified finding.
